extracted.intended_audience: comedians, comedy writers, and humor scholars
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing and evaluating transgressive or shock comedy—when it works, techniques for delivery, critical tensions, forms, and failure modes. Focuses on ethical/aesthetic conditions (audience distance, persona, power dynamics) that determine success or harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Norm transgression
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the joke transgress a norm? Transgressive comedy invites amusement in things typically considered off-limits — events that would normally bring anger, sympathy, or outrage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion: the material must violate an expectation or taboo. Anti-pattern: material that avoids genuine norm-violation (i.e., faux transgression) or uses obvious, safe gags that do not actually test boundaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience distance / consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the audience appropriately distant? The audience must consent (right venue) and have sufficient psychological/social distance (BVT-style) for the transgression to register as comedy rather than harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: choose venues and contexts where the audience expects/accepts edgy material; failing to secure consent or distance is a primary cause of failure (wrong audience).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedian has earned the right
rubrics_metrics.description: Has the comedian earned the right (persona / context)? The performer’s persona, history, and commitment determine whether transgression is read as legitimate rather than exploitative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: develop and maintain a consistent persona (no winking). Earning it can come from established authority, previous work, or contextual framing; lack of earned credibility undermines risky material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shock illuminates rather than merely shocks
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the shock illuminate or just shock? Successful transgressive comedy uses shock to reveal insight, provoke thought, or expose a truth rather than providing mere surprise for its own sake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring note: prioritize material where the transgression generates commentary/insight. Anti-pattern: cheap shock without insight leads to failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power asymmetry / punching up vs punching down
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there asymmetric power (punching up vs down)? Evaluate who is the target relative to the comedian and audience; transgression that punches down risks harm and backlash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: favor targets with greater power or institutions (punching up). Be mindful of whose distance counts, and avoid exploiting vulnerable groups (punching down).

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise (violation of expectation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Surprise: the joke achieves a violation of expectation, a key psychological mechanism for humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: structure setups and punchlines to maximize unexpectedness while preserving coherence; overused or telegraphed reversals reduce effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relief (tension release)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relief: the transgression releases social or emotional tension, producing laughter as catharsis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: assess whether laughter functions as release rather than as mockery or cruelty; material that increases tension without release may traumatize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe norm violation
rubrics_metrics.description: Norm violation: social norms are broken, but done 'safely' so the audience can laugh rather than respond with outrage or hurt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: calibrate the degree and framing of norm violation; unsafe or gratuitous violations that expose real vulnerabilities are likely to fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery: timing, body language, pauses, inflection, deadpan
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliberate timing and delivery (body language, pauses, inflection, deadpan) are technical requirements for achieving maximum transgressive impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: use pauses and deadpan to amplify violation; adjust inflection and body language to manage audience reaction. Anti-pattern: poor timing or mismatched delivery flattens the transgression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persona commitment (no winking)
rubrics_metrics.description: Persona commitment: the comedian must commit to the persona and not 'wink' at the audience to provide an escape route from the transgression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: sustained commitment increases stakes and authenticity; occasional winking can undermine perceived sincerity and reduce impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form / type suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: Choice of transgressive form matters: gross-out (bodily disgust), taboo topic (death, sex, atrocity), in-group violation (saying the unspeakable in the room), identity transgression (speaking from a persona that's not yours).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: select a form appropriate to venue, persona, and audience distance. Some forms (identity transgression) carry higher risk and require more justification/skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tightrope balances (funny vs insensitive; cathartic vs harmful; liberating vs traumatizing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedians must balance competing values: funny vs insensitive, cathartic vs harmful, liberating vs traumatizing; subjects may be personal/traumatic for some and distant for others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring guidance: weigh net effect on audience wellbeing and insight. If harm outweighs catharsis or liberation, the material likely fails ethically and artistically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid letting sheer shock overshadow inquiry into taste
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheer shock value can overshadow inquiry into taste — successful transgression engages with taste, not only provocation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: craft material that invites reflection about why it is funny; avoid tactics that rely solely on escalating shock for effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider censorship vs free expression context
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware of the censorship vs free expression debate when assessing transgressive material and its reception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: contextualize material within broader debates about limits and responsibilities; this affects where and how material may be appropriate or defended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whose distance counts / audience positionality
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whose distance gets to count: audience members’ positionalities affect whether a transgression reads as comedy or harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: analyze audience composition and power relations; the same joke may land very differently depending on who is present and their lived experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure mode: wrong audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Wrong audience — performing transgressive material to an audience without consent, expectation, or appropriate distance will cause the joke to fail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: taking edgy material into unsuitable venues or demographics; mitigate by tailoring set and choosing venues carefully.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure mode: real harm visible
rubrics_metrics.description: Real harm visible — if the transgression concretely harms or retraumatizes audience members, the act fails regardless of intent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: avoid material that reopens wounds or targets ongoing suffering; prioritize minimizing visible harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure mode: cheap shock without insight
rubrics_metrics.description: Cheap shock without insight — using shock as an easy gambit without substantive illumination leads to failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: relying on escalating offensiveness rather than crafting a meaningful point; revise to add perspective, critique, or context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure mode: punching down with no awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Punching down with no awareness — targeting less powerful or vulnerable groups without critical framing is a common cause of backlash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: evaluate targets and power imbalances; if punching down, either reconsider or reframe to reduce harm and increase defensibility.
